label: def:CEV
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:CEV}
Let $\mu\in\mathbb{R}$, $\nu>0$ and $\vartheta>0$. A constant elasticity of variance process, first developed by \cite{cox1975notes} and abbreviated as a CEV process, is a process 
$X=\{X_{t}\}_{t\geq 0}$ satisfying
\[
	dX_{t}=\mu X_{t}dt+\nu\big(X_{t}\big)^{\vartheta}dW_{t},\qquad X_{0}=x_{0}>0.
\]
Here $\mu$ is the linear-drift coefficient, $\nu$ is the volatility scale parameter, and $\vartheta$ is the elasticity parameter. For the standard analytical properties of the CEV process, including existence, positivity, boundary behavior, moment properties, and ergodicity, see, e.g., \cite{revuz1999continuous}, \cite{delbaen2002note}, \cite{gontis2011interplay}, \cite{lindsay2012simulation}, \cite{tsumurai2020malliavin}, \cite{ning2025ckls}.

In this paper, we focus on the sublinear-elasticity, mean-decaying regime
\[
	\frac{1}{2}<\vartheta<1,\qquad\mu<0.
\]
where $\vartheta$ is the parameter of interest, while $\mu$ is treated as a known linear-drift parameter. Notably, for this regime of $\vartheta$, the CEV equation admits a pathwise unique global strong solution satisfying
$\mathbb{P}(0\leq X_{t}<\infty\text{ for all }t\geq0)=1$. Starting from $x_{0}>0$, the process can hit $0$ with positive probability, and once it reaches $0$, it remains there thereafter.
head: environment
name: CEV model

label: def:CKLS
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:CKLS}
Let $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, $\sigma>0$ and $k>0$. 
A Chan--Karolyi--Longstaff--Sanders process, first developed by \cite{chan1992empirical} and abbreviated as a CKLS process, is a process $Y=\{Y_{t}\}_{t\geq 0}$ satisfying
\[
	dY_{t}=(a-bY_{t})dt+\sigma(Y_{t})^{k}dW_{t},\qquad Y_{0}=y_{0}>0.
\]
Here $a$ is the constant-drift coefficient and $b$ is the linear-drift coefficient. In the mean-reverting regime $a,b>0$, $b$ is the mean-reversion speed and $a/b$ is the long-run mean. $\sigma$ is the volatility scale parameter, and $k$ is the elasticity parameter. For $a>0$ and $k\in(1/2,1)$, the equation admits a pathwise unique global strong solution satisfying $\mathbb{P}(0<Y_{t}<\infty\text{ for all }t\geq0)=1$. For other analytical properties of the CKLS process, including existence, positivity, boundary behavior, moment properties, and ergodicity, see, e.g., \cite{andersen2007moment}, \cite{tsumurai2020malliavin}, \cite{mishura2022parameter}, \cite{ning2025ckls}.

While the CEV model appears to be a special case of the CKLS model with $a=0$, it has distinct analytical properties. Although the diffusion coefficient degenerates at the origin in both models, for $1/2<\vartheta<1$, the origin is attainable and absorbing for the CEV process, whereas the CKLS process remains strictly positive.

name: CKLS model

label: def:CIR
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:CIR}
Let $\alpha>0$, $\beta>0$ and $\gamma>0$. A Cox--Ingersoll--Ross process, first developed by \cite{cox1985theory} and abbreviated as a CIR process, is a process $Z=\{Z_{t}\}_{t\geq 0}$ satisfying
\[
	dZ_{t}=(\alpha-\beta Z_{t})dt+\gamma\sqrt{Z_{t}}dW_{t},\qquad Z_{0}=z_{0}>0.
\]
Here $\beta$ denotes the mean-reversion speed, $\alpha$ represents the long-run mean multiplied by $\beta$, and $\gamma$ is the volatility scale parameter. For the standard analytical properties of the CIR process, including existence, positivity, boundary behavior, moment properties, and ergodicity, see, e.g., \cite{revuz1999continuous}, \cite{jeanblanc2009mathematical}, \cite{alaya2013asymptotic}, \cite{ning2025ckls}.

Notably, the condition $\alpha>0$ gives an inward drift at $0$ and prevents absorption there; together with $\beta>0$, it yields a unique Gamma invariant distribution and ergodicity. Strict positivity of paths starting from $z_{0}>0$ is ensured by the additional Feller condition $2\alpha\geq\gamma^{2}$.

We also highlight the CEV--CIR correspondence: Let $X$ be the CEV process in Definition~\ref{def:CEV} with $\vartheta\neq1$.
Set $Z_{t}:=X_{t}^{2(1-\vartheta)}$ and $\tau_{0}:=\inf\{t\geq0:X_{t}=0\}$. Then, for $t<\tau_{0}$, following from It\^{o}'s formula applied to $x\mapsto x^{2(1-\vartheta)}$ localized on compact subintervals of $(0,\infty)$, $Z$ satisfies the following CIR-type dynamics, whose drift parameters need not satisfy the positivity conditions in Definition~\ref{def:CIR}:
\begin{equation}\label{prop:CEV-CIR}
    dZ_{t}=(\alpha_{\vartheta}-\beta_{\vartheta}Z_{t})dt+\gamma_{\vartheta}\sqrt{Z_{t}}dB_{t},\text{ where }\alpha_{\vartheta}=\nu^{2}(1-\vartheta)(1-2\vartheta),~\beta_{\vartheta}=-2\mu(1-\vartheta),~\gamma_{\vartheta}=2\nu|1-\vartheta|,
\end{equation}
$B_{t}=\operatorname{sgn}(1-\vartheta)W_{t}$ is a standard Brownian motion. This power transform is a scaled square of the Lamperti coordinate
\[
    \ell_{\vartheta}(x)=\frac{x^{1-\vartheta}}{\nu(1-\vartheta)},\qquad x^{2(1-\vartheta)}=\nu^{2}(1-\vartheta)^{2}\ell_{\vartheta}(x)^{2}.
\]
Consequently, the CEV process admits the power representation
$X_{t}=Z_{t}^{1/[2(1-\vartheta)]}$ before $\tau_{0}$. This CIR-type representation does not guarantee strict positivity for all times: when $1/2<\vartheta<1$, $\alpha_{\vartheta}<0$ and $2\alpha_{\vartheta}-\gamma_{\vartheta}^{2}=-2\nu^{2}(1-\vartheta)<0$, so the CIR-type diffusion admits a negative constant-drift and the Feller condition is not satisfied.

label: ass:A1
body_md:
\label{ass:A1}
Take the target small-noise CEV process $X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}$ to be the nonnegative CEV solution absorbed at $0$. It is observed at the equidistant grid points, with a finite observation horizon $T>0$,
\[
    t_{i}:=i\Delta_{n},\qquad i=0,1,\ldots,n,\qquad\Delta_{n}:=T/n.
\]
The joint asymptotic regime is an increasing sampling frequency and a vanishing noise
\[
    \varepsilon\to0,\qquad n\to\infty \quad (\text{equivalently, }\Delta_{n}\to0).
\]

Of interest is the elasticity parameter $\vartheta_{0}$ of the small-noise CEV model, satisfying
\[
    1/2<\underline{\vartheta}<\vartheta_{0}<\overline{\vartheta}<1,\qquad\Theta:=[\underline{\vartheta},\overline{\vartheta}].
\]
Moreover, $\mu<0$, $\nu>0$, and $x_{0}>0$ are assumed to be known and fixed constants.

    a_{\varepsilon}:=\varepsilon^{2}a^{*}>0,\qquad\text{for each }\varepsilon>0.

This regularization is used in the auxiliary CKLS process introduced in \eqref{Local-to-CEV-CKLS}.

body_md:

\[
    j_{n}:=\lfloor\tau/\Delta_{n}\rfloor,\qquad\tau_{n}:=t_{j_{n}},\qquad h_{n}:=m_{n}\Delta_{n},
\]
where $m_{n}$ is a sequence of positive integers such that
$\tau'_{n}:=\tau_{n}+h_{n}\leq T$. Then $\tau_{n}\to\tau$. The local window $h_{n}$ satisfies
\[
    h_{n}\to0,\qquad m_{n}\to\infty,\qquad (\text{or equivalently,}\quad\Delta_{n}/h_{n}=1/m_{n}\to0).
\]
Moreover, choose $\tau$ such that $|\log\mathcal{X}_{\tau}|\geq c_{0}$ for some constant $c_{0}>0$, where $\mathcal{X}_{t}:=x_{0}e^{\mu t},~0\leq t\leq T$, denotes the deterministic small-noise limit of the target small-noise CEV model.

label: auxiliary-oracle-limit-main-proof
title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:auxiliary-oracle-lse}, the auxiliary CIR oracle has a first-order limit under $\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}$. The local-to-CEV scaling
gives total-variation closeness between $\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}$ and $\mathbb{P}$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:total-variation-closeness}). Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer-convergence} therefore yields
\begin{equation}\label{auxiliary-oracle-limit-main-proof}
    \varepsilon^{-1}\big(\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}-\beta_{0}\big)\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}\text{-prob.}}\xi_{\beta_{0}},\qquad\text{where}\quad\xi_{\beta_{0}}=-2\nu(1-\vartheta_{0})\frac{\int_{0}^{T}\mathcal{X}_{t}^{3-3\vartheta_{0}}dW_{t}}{\int_{0}^{T}\mathcal{X}_{t}^{4-4\vartheta_{0}}dt}.
\end{equation}
Here Assumption~\ref{ass:A5} implies the required oracle discretization condition $\Delta_{n}=o(\varepsilon)$.

Next, Theorem~\ref{thm:auxiliary-cev-oracle-equivalence} gives the path-replacement bound
\begin{equation}\label{auxiliary-cev-equivalence-main-proof}
    \widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{X,\circ}-\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}=o_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon),
\end{equation}
For the plug-in step, Theorem~\ref{thm:preliminary-estimator-rate} and Assumptions~\ref{ass:A4},~\ref{ass:A5} give
\[
	\widetilde{\vartheta}_{\varepsilon,n}-\vartheta_{0}=o_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon).
\]
Together with the uniform parameter-sensitivity bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:plugin-equivalence}, this implies
\begin{equation}\label{plugin-equivalence-main-proof}
    \widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}-\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{X,\circ}=o_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon).
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{auxiliary-oracle-limit-main-proof}, \eqref{auxiliary-cev-equivalence-main-proof}, and \eqref{plugin-equivalence-main-proof}, 
\[
    \varepsilon^{-1}\big(\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}-\beta_{0}\big)=\varepsilon^{-1}\big(\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}-\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{X,\circ}\big)+\varepsilon^{-1}\big(\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{X,\circ}-\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}\big)+\varepsilon^{-1}\big(\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}-\beta_{0}\big)\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}\text{-prob.}}\xi_{\beta_{0}},
\]
and using \eqref{final-elasticity-estimator} and \eqref{elasticity-beta-relation}, we obtain $\varepsilon^{-1}(\widehat{\vartheta}_{\varepsilon,n}-\vartheta_{0})=(2\mu)^{-1}\varepsilon^{-1}(\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}-\beta_{0})\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}\text{-prob.}}\xi_{\vartheta_{0}}$. Consistency follows because $\varepsilon\to0$. The integrand in \eqref{elasticity-limit-variable} is deterministic, so the limit is centered Gaussian with variance given by  \eqref{elasticity-asymptotic-variance}. \hfill\qedsymbol
head: manual
name: Theorem \refthm:asymptotic-distribution

title: Remark
body_md:
The CKLS--CIR construction involves inverse powers of the state in both the transformed dynamics and the Girsanov kernel, requiring control near $0$ when transferring asymptotic results to the absorbing CEV model with $1/2<\vartheta<1$. Define $\tau_{0}^{\varepsilon}:=\inf\{t\geq0:X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}=0\}$. After localization away from $0$, It\^{o}'s formula applied to $Z_{t}^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}=\mathcal{T}(X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}};\vartheta_{0})$ gives, for $t<\tau_{0}^{\varepsilon}$,
\[
    dZ_{t}^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}=\big(\alpha_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{CEV}}-\beta_{0}Z_{t}^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}\big)dt+\varepsilon\nu\zeta\sqrt{Z_{t}^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}}dW_{t},\qquad\text{where}\quad    \alpha_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{CEV}}=\frac{\varepsilon^{2}\nu^{2}\zeta^{2}(1-2\vartheta_{0})}{4(1-\vartheta_{0})}<0,
\]
and $\beta_{0}=-2\mu(1-\vartheta_{0})>0$. As noted in the property \eqref{prop:CEV-CIR}, this CIR-type identity has negative constant-drift and does not provide the strictly positive CIR benchmark required by our measure-change construction. It cannot hold unchanged beyond $\tau_{0}^{\varepsilon}$: the mapped process remains at $0$ after absorption, whereas the displayed drift at $0$ is $\alpha_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{CEV}}<0$. The absorbed continuation therefore requires a stopped formulation. Moreover, an equivalent change of measure cannot eliminate a positive-probability event on which the same mapped process hits $0$. The auxiliary construction in Subsection~\ref{subsec:local-to-cev} instead applies the CKLS--CIR transform of Appendix~\ref{aaa} to a strictly positive auxiliary process, providing the strictly positive CIR benchmark for localized oracle asymptotics.

name: Direct CEV mapping and the zero boundary

label: lem:ckls-density-martingale
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:ckls-density-martingale}
For $k\in(1/2,1)$ and $T<\infty$, the stochastic exponential $\Lambda$ defined in \eqref{girsanov-kernel-general} is a strictly positive $\mathbb{P}$-martingale on $[0,T]$, with $\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}[\Lambda_{t}]=1$ for all $0\leq t\leq T$. Consequently, $d\mathbb{Q}/d\mathbb{P}|_{\mathcal{F}_{T}}=\Lambda_{T}$ defines an equivalent probability measure under which $\widetilde{W}$ is a standard Brownian motion on $[0,T]$.
head: environment
name: Validity of the measure change

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $J=(0,\infty)$, $m(y)=a-by$, $\Sigma(y)=\sigma y^{k}$. Since $\Sigma>0$ and $m,\Sigma,q$ are continuous on $J$, $\Sigma^{-2},m\Sigma^{-2},q^{2}\Sigma^{-2}\in L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(J)$ (Engelbert--Schmidt conditions). The auxiliary diffusion associated with the integrand $-q$, initially defined up to exit from $J$, has diffusion coefficient $\Sigma$ and drift
\[
	\check m(y):=m(y)-q(y)\Sigma(y)=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2}y^{2k-1}-by.
\]
Its scale density, normalized at $1$, is
\[
	\check{\rho}(y)=\exp\Big\{-\int_{1}^{y}\frac{2\check m(z)}{(\Sigma(z))^{2}}dz\Big\}=\frac{1}{y}\exp\Big\{\mathcal{M}\big(y^{2(1-k)}-1\big)\Big\},\qquad\mathcal{M}:=\frac{b}{\sigma^{2}(1-k)}>0.
\]
Since $\check{\rho}(y)\geq e^{-M}/y$ for $0<y\leq1$ and $\check{\rho}(y)\geq1/y$ for $y\geq1$, its scale integrals diverge at both endpoints. Feller's explosion test therefore excludes exit of the auxiliary diffusion from $J$. The original diffusion also remains in $J$. Thus, \cite[Corollary~2.2]{mijatovic2012martingale}, applied with integrand $-q$, shows that $\Lambda$ is a true martingale on $[0,T]$. Since $\Lambda_{0}=1$, $\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}[\Lambda_{t}]=1$ for all $0\leq t\leq T$. The final assertion follows from the strict positivity of $\Lambda_{T}$ and Girsanov's theorem.

By \cite{ning2025ckls}: for $0<k<1/2$, the Yamada--Watanabe criterion does not apply, and $0$ is attainable; the singularities of $\partial_{yy}\mathcal{T}$ and the Girsanov kernel in \eqref{girsanov-kernel-general} require localization and separate boundary analysis. head: environment
name: Parameter restrictions

label: lem:uniform-inverse-moment-small-noise
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:uniform-inverse-moment-small-noise}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:A2} and~\ref{ass:A3}, for every $r>0$, $T\in(0,\infty)$, and $\varepsilon_{0}\in(0,1]$, there exists a constant $C_{r,T,\varepsilon_{0}}=C(r,T,\varepsilon_{0},a^{*},\mu,\nu,\vartheta_{0},x_{0})<\infty$ such that
\[
    \sup_{0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_{0}}\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\big[\big(Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{-r}\big]\leq C_{r,T,\varepsilon_{0}}.
\]
head: environment
name: Uniform inverse-moment bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f_{r}(y)=y^{-r}$ and stop $Y^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}$ at its exit time $\tau_{m}^{\varepsilon}$ from $(m^{-1},m)$, $m>\max\{x_{0},x_{0}^{-1}\}$. Its generator satisfies
\[
    \mathcal{L}^{\varepsilon}f_{r}(y)=-r\mu y^{-r}+\varepsilon^{2}\big[-ra^{*}y^{-r-1}+\frac{r(r+1)}{2}\nu^{2}y^{-r-2+2\vartheta_{0}}\big].
\]
With $x=y^{-r-1}$ and $\rho_{r}=(r+2-2\vartheta_{0})/(r+1)\in(0,1)$, the bracket equals $-ra^{*}x+\frac{r(r+1)}2\nu^{2}x^{\rho_{r}}\leq C_{r}$ for some $C_{r}>0$. Thus, for $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_{0}$, $\mathcal{L}^{\varepsilon}f_{r}\leq r|\mu|f_{r}+\varepsilon_{0}^{2}C_{r}$. The stopped It\^{o} formula and Gr\"{o}nwall's inequality give
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\big[f_{r}\big(Y_{t\wedge\tau_{m}^{\varepsilon}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)\big]\leq\big(x_{0}^{-r}+\varepsilon_{0}^{2}C_{r}T\big)e^{r|\mu|T},\qquad 0\leq t\leq T.
\]
For each $\varepsilon>0$, strict positivity and non-explosion imply $\tau_{m}^{\varepsilon}\uparrow\infty~a.s.$. Fatou's lemma yields the claimed result.
head: environment

label: thm:total-variation-closeness
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:total-variation-closeness}
Under the conditions of
Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-inverse-moment-small-noise},
as $\varepsilon\to0$,
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\int_{0}^{T}\big|q_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big|^{2}dt\Big]=O(\varepsilon^{2}),\qquad\|\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}-\mathbb{P}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\big[|\Lambda_{T}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}-1|\big]=O(\varepsilon).
\]
Consequently, $\Lambda_{T}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\to1$ in $L^{1}(\mathbb{P})$ and $\log\Lambda_{T}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\to0$ in $\mathbb{P}$-probability.
head: environment
name: Girsanov energy and asymptotic measure closeness

title: Proof
body_md:
With the inequality $|x+y|^{2}\leq 2|x|^{2}+2|y|^{2}$, the kernel representation and Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-inverse-moment-small-noise} give
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\int_{0}^{T}\big|q_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big|^{2}dt\Big]\leq C\varepsilon^{2}\int_{0}^{T}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\big(Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{-2\vartheta_{0}}+\big(Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{-2(1-\vartheta_{0})}\Big]dt\leq C_{T}\varepsilon^{2}.
\]
Thus, $\int_{0}^{T}q_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}dW_{t}$ is square-integrable with mean $0$. Let $H(\mathbb{P}\mid\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}):=\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}[-\log\Lambda_{T}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}]$ denote the relative entropy (Kullback–Leibler divergence). The density formula in \eqref{girsanov-kernel-general} and Pinsker's inequality yield
\[
    \|\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}-\mathbb{P}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}^{2}\leq\frac{1}{2} H(\mathbb{P}\mid\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon})=\frac{1}{4}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\int_{0}^{T}\big|q_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big|^{2}dt\Big]=O(\varepsilon^{2}).
\]
The stated $L^{1}$ bound follows from $\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}[|\Lambda_{T}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}-1|]=2\|\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}-\mathbb{P}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}$. Finally, convergence of $\log\Lambda_{T}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}$ follows from convergence of $\Lambda_{T}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}$ in probability and continuity of the logarithm at $1$.

label: thm:transfer-convergence
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:transfer-convergence}
Under the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:total-variation-closeness}, let
$(\mathsf{E},d_{\mathsf{E}})$ be a Polish space. For any $\mathsf{E}$-valued, $\mathcal{F}_{T}$-measurable random elements $U_{\varepsilon,n}$ and $U$,
\[
	U_{\varepsilon,n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}\text{-prob.}}U\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad U_{\varepsilon,n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}\text{-prob.}}U.
\]
Moreover, weak convergence under $\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}$ is equivalent to weak convergence to the same limiting law under $\mathbb{P}$.
head: environment
name: Transfer of convergence

title: Proof
body_md:
For every $\eta>0$, define $A_{\varepsilon,n}(\eta):=\{d_{\mathsf{E}}(U_{\varepsilon,n},U)>\eta\}\in\mathcal{F}_{T}$, then
\[
	\big|\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}(A_{\varepsilon,n}(\eta))-\mathbb{P}(A_{\varepsilon,n}(\eta))\big|\leq \|\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}-\mathbb{P}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0,\qquad\text{as}\quad\varepsilon\to0,
\]
which proves the probability statement. The weak-convergence statement follows similarly from the total-variation bound for expectations of bounded continuous functions.

label: lem:local-to-CEV-process-approx
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:local-to-CEV-process-approx}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:A2} and~\ref{ass:A3}, fix $T\in(0,\infty)$. For any $\vartheta\in\Theta$, suppose that $X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}$ and $Y^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}$ are defined on the same filtered probability space, driven by the same Brownian motion $W$, and solve \eqref{small-noise-CEV-def} and \eqref{Local-to-CEV-CKLS}, respectively. For fixed $0<\delta<M<\infty$, define the compact localization event
\[
    \Omega_{\delta,M}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}:=\Big\{\delta\leq\inf_{0\leq t\leq T}\min\{Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta},X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\}\leq\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\max\{Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta},X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\}\leq M \Big\}.
\]
Then there exists a constant $C_{\delta,M,T}>0$, independent of $\varepsilon$, such that
\[
	\mathbb{E}\big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\big|Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}-X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big|^{2}\mathds{1}_{\Omega_{\delta,M}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}}\big]\leq C_{\delta,M,T}\varepsilon^{4},\quad\text{and consequently, }\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\big|Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}-X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big|\mathds{1}_{\Omega_{\delta,M}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}}=O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{2}).
\]
head: environment
name: Process-level local-to-CEV approximation

label: L2-estimate-D
title: Proof
body_md:
Set $D_{t}:=Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}-X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}$ and
$\tau:=\inf\{t\geq0:(X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta},Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta})
\notin(\delta/2,2M)^{2}\}$. On $[\delta/2,2M]$, the map $x\mapsto x^\vartheta$ is Lipschitz uniformly in $\vartheta\in\Theta$. Subtracting the two SDEs, stopping at $\tau$, and applying the Cauchy--Schwarz and BDG inequalities therefore give,
for $0\leq t\leq T$ and $0<\varepsilon\leq1$,
\[
    \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{0\leq r\leq t}|D_{r\wedge\tau}|^{2}\Big]\leq C\varepsilon^{4}+C\int_{0}^{t}\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{0\leq r\leq s}|D_{r\wedge\tau}|^{2}\Big]ds,
\]
where $C$ is independent of $\varepsilon$ and $\vartheta$. Since $\tau>T$ on $\Omega_{\delta,M}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}$, Gr\"{o}nwall's inequality yields
\begin{equation}\label{L2-estimate-D}
    \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}|D_{t}|^{2}\mathds{1}_{\Omega_{\delta,M}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}}\Big]\leq\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}|D_{t\wedge\tau}|^{2}\Big]\leq C_{\delta,M,T}\varepsilon^{4}.
\end{equation}
The stated $O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{2})$ bound follows from Markov's inequality.

label: lem:uniform-deterministic-limit
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:uniform-deterministic-limit}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:A1},~\ref{ass:A2},~\ref{ass:A3}, for any $\vartheta\in\Theta$,
\[
	\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\big|X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}-\mathcal{X}_{t}\big|=O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon),\qquad
	\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\big|Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}-\mathcal{X}_{t}\big|=O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon).
\]
head: environment
name: Uniform deterministic small-noise limit

label: X-Y-uniform-second-moment
title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{Step~1 (Uniform moment bounds)}: For $m>x_{0}$, let $\tau_{m}:=\inf\{t\geq0:\max(X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta},Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta})\geq m\}$. The stopped It\^{o} formulas have bounded stochastic integrands and hence mean-zero martingale terms. Using $x^{2\vartheta}\leq1+x^{2}$ and $2a^{*}x\leq(a^{*})^{2}+x^{2}$, we obtain, for $0<\varepsilon\leq1$ and $t\leq T$,
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\big[\big(X_{t\wedge\tau_{m}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big)^{2}+(Y_{t\wedge\tau_{m}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big)^{2}\big]\leq 2x_{0}^{2}+C\int_{0}^{t}\Big[1+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\big[\big(X_{s\wedge\tau_{m}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big)^{2}+\big(Y_{s\wedge\tau_{m}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big)^{2}\big]\Big]ds,
\]
where $C$ is independent of $m$, $\varepsilon$, $\vartheta$. Gr\"{o}nwall's inequality and Fatou's lemma, using nonexplosion to let $m\to\infty$, yield
\begin{equation}\label{X-Y-uniform-second-moment}
    \sup_{0<\varepsilon\leq1}\sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\big[\big(X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big)^{2}+\big(Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big)^{2}\big]\leq C_{T}<\infty.
\end{equation}

\textbf{Step~2 (Approximation by the deterministic path)}: Variation of constants gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
    X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}-\mathcal{X}_{t}=\varepsilon\nu e^{\mu t}\int_{0}^{t}e^{-\mu s}\big(X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big)^{\vartheta}dW_{s},\qquad
    Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}-\mathcal{X}_{t}=\varepsilon^{2}a^{*}e^{\mu t}\int_{0}^{t}e^{-\mu s}ds+\varepsilon\nu e^{\mu t}\int_{0}^{t}e^{-\mu s}\big(Y_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big)^{\vartheta}dW_{s}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $e^{\pm\mu t}$ are bounded on $[0,T]$, the BDG inequality, $x^{2\vartheta}\leq1+x^{2}$, and \eqref{X-Y-uniform-second-moment} imply
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\big(\big|X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}-\mathcal{X}_{t}\big|^{2}+\big|Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}-\mathcal{X}_{t}\big|^{2}\big)\Big]\leq C_{T}\varepsilon^{4}+C_{T}\varepsilon^{2}\int_{0}^{T}\Big[1+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\big[\big(X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big)^{2}+\big(Y_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta}\big)^{2}\big]\Big]ds\leq C_{T}\varepsilon^{2},
\]
uniformly in $\vartheta\in\Theta$. Both assertions follow from Markov's inequality.

head: environment
name: Moment and increment bounds for $Z_{u}^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ}$

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $Z_{t}=Z_{t}^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ}$ and $z_{0}=Z_{0}$. For $m>z_{0}$, let
$\tau_{m}=\inf\{t\geq0:Z_{t}\geq m\}$. Applying It\^{o}'s formula to $(Z_{t\wedge\tau_{m}})^{p}$, $p=1,2,3$, and taking expectations, the stopped martingale
term has mean $0$. Dropping the nonpositive drift term and using $\alpha_{\varepsilon}=O(\varepsilon^{2})$ gives
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}\Big[\big(Z_{t\wedge\tau_{m}}\big)^{p}\Big]\leq z_{0}^{p}+C\varepsilon^{2}\int_{0}^{t}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}\Big[\big(Z_{v\wedge\tau_{m}}\big)^{p-1}\Big]dv,\qquad p=1,2,3,
\]
where $Z^{0}=1$ and $C$ is independent of $\varepsilon$ and $m$. Induction over $p$ yields moment bounds uniform in $t\in[0,T]$, $m$, and $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_{0}$. Nonexplosion and Fatou's lemma then give the asserted bounds for $Z_{t}$.

For $0\leq s\leq u\leq T$, the SDE, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, and It\^{o}'s isometry yield
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}\big[|Z_u-Z_s|^{2}\big]\leq 2(u-s)\int_{s}^{u}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}\big[|\alpha_{\varepsilon}-\beta_{0}Z_{v}|^{2}\big]dv+2\varepsilon^{2}\gamma^{2}\int_{s}^{u}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}[Z_{v}]dv\leq C\big((u-s)^{2}+\varepsilon^{2}(u-s)\big),
\]
by the uniform first- and second-moment bounds.

label: thm:auxiliary-oracle-lse
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:auxiliary-oracle-lse}
Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{ass:A1},~\ref{ass:A2},~\ref{ass:A3} hold, together with $\Delta_{n}=o(\varepsilon)$. Then the auxiliary oracle estimator $\widehat{\beta}^{Y,\circ}_{\varepsilon,n}$ satisfies
\[
      \widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}\text{-prob.}}\beta_{0}\quad\text{and}\quad\varepsilon^{-1}\big(\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}-\beta_{0}\big)\xrightarrow{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}\text{-prob.}}\xi_{\beta_{0}},\quad\text{where}\quad\xi_{\beta_{0}}:=-\gamma\frac{\int_{0}^{T}(\mathcal{Z}_{t})^{3/2}dW_{t}}{\int_{0}^{T}(\mathcal{Z}_{t})^{2}dt}.
\]
Moreover, $\xi_{\beta_{0}}$ is $\mathcal{F}_{T}$-measurable and $\mathcal{L}_{\mathbb{P}}(\xi_{\beta_{0}})=\mathcal{N}(0,V_{\beta_{0}})$, where $V_{\beta_{0}}=\big(\gamma^{2}\int_{0}^{T}(\mathcal{Z}_{t})^{3}dt\big)\big/\big(\int_{0}^{T}(\mathcal{Z}_{t})^{2}dt\big)^{2}$.
head: environment
name: Oracle LSE under the Auxiliary Measure

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $Z_{t}=Z_{t}^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ}$ and let $\eta_{n}(s)=t_{i-1}$ for $s\in(t_{i-1},t_{i}]$. 

\textbf{Step~1 (Error decomposition)}: For $\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, define the unweighted Euler contrast
\[
    \Psi_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}(\beta):=\frac{1}{\varepsilon^{2}\Delta_{n}}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big[\Delta_{i}Z-(\alpha_{\varepsilon}-\beta Z_{t_{i-1}})\Delta_{n}\big]^{2}.
\]
Differentiation gives
\[
    \partial_{\beta}\Psi_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}(\beta)=\frac{2}{\varepsilon^{2}}\sum_{i=1}^{n}Z_{t_{i-1}}\big[\Delta_{i}Z-\alpha_{\varepsilon}\Delta_{n}+\beta Z_{t_{i-1}}\Delta_{n}\big],\qquad\partial_{\beta}^{2}\Psi_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}(\beta)=\frac{2\Delta_{n}}{\varepsilon^{2}}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(Z_{t_{i-1}}\big)^{2}>0,
\]
where strict positivity follows from $Z_{0}>0$. Thus, solving $\partial_{\beta}\Psi_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}(\beta)=0$ gives the unique minimizer $\widehat\beta_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}=\mathcal{B}_{\varepsilon,n}(Z)$ defined by \eqref{path-functional-B}. Define
\[
    D_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}:=\int_{0}^{T}\big(Z_{\eta_{n}(s)}\big)^{2}ds,\qquad
    M_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}:=\int_{0}^{T}Z_{\eta_{n}(s)}\sqrt{Z_{s}}d\widetilde{W}_{s}^{\varepsilon},\qquad 
    R_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}:=-\beta_{0}\int_{0}^{T}Z_{\eta_{n}(s)}(Z_{s}-Z_{\eta_{n}(s)})ds.
\]
Substituting \eqref{auxiliary-oracle-cir-dynamics} into \eqref{path-functional-B} gives
\begin{equation}\label{contrast-derived-normalized-error}
    \varepsilon^{-1}(\widehat\beta_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}-\beta_{0})=-\gamma\frac{M_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}}{D_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}}-\frac{R_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}}{\varepsilon D_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}},
\end{equation}
where $D_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}\geq\Delta_{n}(Z_{0})^{2}>0$.

\textbf{Step~2 (Denominator and remainder)}: Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-deterministic-limit}, local Lipschitz continuity of $\mathcal{T}(\cdot;\vartheta_{0})$ near the positive trajectory $\mathcal{X}$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer-convergence} yield $\sup_{t\leq T}|Z_{t}-\mathcal{Z}_{t}|=o_{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}(1)$. Since $\mathcal{Z}$ is continuous and strictly positive,
\begin{equation}\label{contrast-denominator-limit}
    D_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}\text{-prob.}}D_{0}:=\int_{0}^{T}\big(\mathcal{Z}_{t}\big)^{2}dt>0.
\end{equation}
By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and the moment and increment bounds in Lemma~\ref{lem:auxiliary-pseudo-cir-bounds},
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}\big[|R_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}|\big]\leq C\int_{0}^{T}\big[(s-\eta_{n}(s))^{2}+\varepsilon^{2}(s-\eta_{n}(s))\big]^{1/2}ds\leq C(\Delta_{n}+\varepsilon\sqrt{\Delta_{n}}).
\]
Consequently, $\Delta_{n}=o(\varepsilon)$ implies $\varepsilon^{-1}R_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}=O_{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}(\Delta_{n}/\varepsilon+\sqrt{\Delta_{n}})=o_{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}(1)$.

\textbf{Step~3 (Martingale approximation)}: Set $H_{\varepsilon,n}(s):=Z_{\eta_{n}(s)}\sqrt{Z_{s}}-(\mathcal{Z}_{s})^{3/2}$. The uniform convergence in \textbf{Step~2} and continuity of $\mathcal{Z}$ imply $\sup_{s\leq T}|H_{\varepsilon,n}(s)|=o_{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}(1)$. Thus, the continuous local martingale
$N_{\varepsilon,n}(t):=\int_{0}^{t}H_{\varepsilon,n}(s)d\widetilde{W}_{s}^{\varepsilon}$ satisfies $\langle N_{\varepsilon,n}\rangle_{T}=\int_{0}^{T}|H_{\varepsilon,n}(s)|^{2}ds=o_{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}(1)$. Lenglart's inequality therefore gives
\begin{equation}\label{oracle-martingale-tildeW}
    M_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}=\int_{0}^{T}\big(\mathcal{Z}_{s}\big)^{3/2}d\widetilde{W}_{s}^{\varepsilon}+o_{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}(1).
\end{equation}

\textbf{Step~4 (Measure transfer and conclusion)}: Since $d\widetilde{W}_{s}^{\varepsilon}=dW_{s}+q_{s}^{\varepsilon}ds$,
\[
    \int_{0}^{T}\big(\mathcal{Z}_{s}\big)^{3/2}d\widetilde{W}_{s}^{\varepsilon}=\int_{0}^{T}\big(\mathcal{Z}_{s}\big)^{3/2}dW_{s}+\int_{0}^{T}\big(\mathcal{Z}_{s}\big)^{3/2}q_{s}^{\varepsilon}ds.
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:total-variation-closeness} and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\Big|\int_{0}^{T}(\mathcal{Z}_{s})^{3/2}q_{s}^{\varepsilon}ds\Big|^{2}\Big]\leq\Big[\int_{0}^{T}\big(\mathcal{Z}_{s}\big)^{3}ds\Big]\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\int_{0}^{T}\big|q_{s}^{\varepsilon}\big|^{2}ds\Big]=O(\varepsilon^{2}).
\]
The correction is therefore $o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ and, by Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer-convergence}, $o_{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}(1)$. Hence,
\[
    M_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}=\int_{0}^{T}\big(\mathcal{Z}_{s}\big)^{3/2}dW_{s}+o_{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}(1).
\]
Combining the preceding estimates with \eqref{contrast-derived-normalized-error} yields
\[
    \varepsilon^{-1}(\widehat\beta_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}-\beta_{0})\xrightarrow{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}\text{-prob.}}-\gamma\frac{\int_{0}^{T}(\mathcal{Z}_{s})^{3/2}dW_{s}}{D_{0}}=\xi_{\beta_{0}}.
\]
Moreover, \eqref{oracle-martingale-tildeW} gives $M_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y}=O_{\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon}}(1)$, so \eqref{contrast-derived-normalized-error} also yields consistency. Since $\mathcal{Z}$ is deterministic, $\xi_{\beta_{0}}$ is $\mathcal{F}_{T}$-measurable and has the stated Gaussian law under $\mathbb{P}$.

name: Auxiliary-to-CEV oracle equivalence

label: transformed-xy-path-difference
title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{Step~1 (Localization and denominator comparison)}: Choose $0<\delta<\inf_{t\leq T}\mathcal{X}_{t}$ and $M>\sup_{t\leq T}\mathcal{X}_{t}$, define
\[
	\tau^{\varepsilon}:=\inf\big\{t\geq0:\big(X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}},Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)\notin(\delta,M)^{2}\big\},\qquad\delta Z_{t}^{\varepsilon}:=Z_{t}^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}-Z_{t}^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-deterministic-limit} gives $\mathbb{P}(\tau^{\varepsilon}\leq T)\to0$. The stopped $L^{2}$ argument in Lemma~\ref{lem:local-to-CEV-process-approx}, together with the local Lipschitz continuity of $\mathcal{T}(\cdot;\vartheta_{0})$, yields
\begin{equation}\label{transformed-xy-path-difference}
	\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sup_{t\leq T}|\delta Z_{t\wedge\tau^{\varepsilon}}^{\varepsilon}|^{2}\Big]\leq C\varepsilon^{4},\qquad\sup_{t\leq T}|\delta Z_{t}^{\varepsilon}|=O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{2}).
\end{equation}
The second assertion follows from Markov's inequality and $\mathbb{P}(\tau^{\varepsilon}\leq T)\to0$, since the stopped and unstopped paths coincide on $\{\tau^{\varepsilon}>T\}$. Both transformed paths are also bounded in probability uniformly on $[0,T]$.

For a discrete path $V=\{V_{t_{i}}\}_{i=0}^{n}$, write
\[
	\mathfrak{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(V):=\alpha_{\varepsilon}\Delta_{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}V_{t_{i-1}}-\sum_{i=1}^{n}V_{t_{i-1}}\Delta_{i}V,\qquad\mathfrak{D}_{n}(V):=\Delta_{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(V_{t_{i-1}})^{2}.
\]
The two oracle estimators are the corresponding ratios $\mathfrak{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(V)/\mathfrak{D}_{n}(V)$. Since $n\Delta_{n}=T$, \eqref{transformed-xy-path-difference} implies
\[
	\mathfrak{D}_{n}(Z^{X,\varepsilon,\circ})-\mathfrak{D}_{n}(Z^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ})=O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{2}).
\]
Moreover, \eqref{contrast-denominator-limit} and Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer-convergence} give $\mathfrak{D}_{n}(Z^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ})\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}\text{-prob.}}D_{0}:=\int_{0}^{T}(\mathcal{Z}_{t})^{2}dt>0$. Thus, $\mathfrak{D}_{n}(Z^{X,\varepsilon,\circ})$ has the same limit, and its reciprocal is $O_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$.

\textbf{Step~2 (Squared-increment comparison)}: Under $\mathbb{P}$, It\^{o}'s formula before $\tau^{\varepsilon}$ gives $d\delta Z_{t}^{\varepsilon}=m_{t}^{\varepsilon}dt+\Sigma_{t}^{\varepsilon}dW_{t}$, where
\[
	m_{t}^{\varepsilon}:=-\beta_{0}\delta Z_{t}^{\varepsilon}-\varepsilon^{2}a^{*}\frac{\zeta^{2}}{2(1-\vartheta_{0})}\big(Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{1-2\vartheta_{0}},\qquad\Sigma_{t}^{\varepsilon}:=\varepsilon\gamma\Big(\sqrt{Z_{t}^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}}-\sqrt{Z_{t}^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ}}\Big).
\]
On $[0,T\wedge\tau^{\varepsilon}]$, $\big(Y_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{1-2\vartheta_{0}}$ is bounded, so $|m_{t}^{\varepsilon}|^{2}\leq C\big(|\delta Z_{t}^{\varepsilon}|^{2}+\varepsilon^{4}\big)$. Moreover, $|\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{y}|^{2}\leq|x-y|$ gives $|\Sigma_{t}^{\varepsilon}|^{2}\leq\varepsilon^{2}\gamma^{2}|\delta Z_{t}^{\varepsilon}|$. Thus, \eqref{transformed-xy-path-difference} and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\int_{0}^{T\wedge\tau^{\varepsilon}}\big|m_{s}^{\varepsilon}\big|^{2}ds\Big]&\leq C\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sup_{t\leq T}|\delta Z_{t\wedge\tau^{\varepsilon}}^{\varepsilon}|^{2}\Big]+C\varepsilon^{4}\leq C\varepsilon^{4},\\
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\int_{0}^{T\wedge\tau^{\varepsilon}}\big|\Sigma_{s}^{\varepsilon}\big|^{2}ds\Big]&\leq C\varepsilon^{2}\Big\{\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sup_{t\leq T}|\delta Z_{t\wedge\tau^{\varepsilon}}^{\varepsilon}|^{2}\Big]\Big\}^{1/2}\leq C\varepsilon^{4}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and It\^{o}'s isometry therefore yield
\[
	\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big|\delta Z_{t_{i}\wedge\tau^{\varepsilon}}^{\varepsilon}-\delta Z_{t_{i-1}\wedge\tau^{\varepsilon}}^{\varepsilon}\big|^{2}\Big]\leq 2\Delta_{n}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\int_{0}^{T\wedge\tau^{\varepsilon}}|m_{s}^{\varepsilon}|^{2}ds\Big]+2\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\int_{0}^{T\wedge\tau^{\varepsilon}}|\Sigma_{s}^{\varepsilon}|^{2}ds\Big]\leq C\varepsilon^{4}.
\]
By Markov's inequality and $\mathbb{P}(\tau^{\varepsilon}\leq T)\to0$,
\begin{equation}\label{realized-qv-delta-Z-bound}
	\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(\Delta_{i}\delta Z^{\varepsilon}\big)^{2}=O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{4}).
\end{equation}
Similarly, the SDEs, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, It\^{o}'s isometry, and \eqref{X-Y-uniform-second-moment}, using $x^{2\vartheta_{0}}\leq1+x^{2}$, give
\[
	\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(|\Delta_{i}X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}|^{2}+|\Delta_{i}Y^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}|^{2}\big)\Big]\leq C(\varepsilon^{2}+\Delta_{n}).
\]
On $\{\tau^{\varepsilon}>T\}$, the mapping $\mathcal{T}(\cdot;\vartheta_{0})$ is Lipschitz on $[\delta,M]$. Hence, Markov's inequality gives
\begin{equation}\label{transformed-process-realized-qv-bound}
	\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big[\big(\Delta_{i}Z^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}\big)^{2}+\big(\Delta_{i}Z^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ}\big)^{2}\Big]=O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{2}+\Delta_{n}).
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{realized-qv-delta-Z-bound} and \eqref{transformed-process-realized-qv-bound} with the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality yields \begin{equation}\label{xy-realized-qv-difference}
	\Big|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big[\big(\Delta_{i}Z^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}\big)^{2}-\big(\Delta_{i}Z^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ}\big)^{2}\Big]\Big|\leq\Big[\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(\Delta_{i}\delta Z^{\varepsilon}\big)^{2}\Big]^{\frac{1}{2}}\Big[\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(\Delta_{i}Z^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}+\Delta_{i}Z^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ}\big)^{2}\Big]^{\frac{1}{2}}=O_{\mathbb{P}}\big(\varepsilon^{2}\sqrt{\varepsilon^{2}+\Delta_{n}}\big).
\end{equation}
\textbf{Step~3 (Numerator comparison and oracle equivalence)}: For any discrete path $V$,
\begin{equation}\label{discrete-integration-by-parts-square}
	\sum_{i=1}^{n}V_{t_{i-1}}\Delta_{i}V=\frac{1}{2}\Big[V_{T}^{2}-V_{0}^{2}-\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\Delta_{i}V)^{2}\Big].
\end{equation}
Since $Z_{0}^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}
=Z_{0}^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ}$,
\eqref{discrete-integration-by-parts-square} gives
\[
    \mathfrak{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(Z^{X,\varepsilon,\circ})-\mathfrak{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(Z^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ})=\alpha_{\varepsilon}\Delta_{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\delta Z_{t_{i-1}}^{\varepsilon}-\frac{1}{2}\Big[\big(Z_{T}^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}\big)^{2}-\big(Z_{T}^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ}\big)^{2}\Big]+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big[\big(\Delta_iZ^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}\big)^{2}-\big(\Delta_iZ^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ}\big)^{2}\Big].
\]
The drift-sum term is $O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{4})$ by $\alpha_{\varepsilon}=O(\varepsilon^{2})$, $n\Delta_{n}=T$, and \eqref{transformed-xy-path-difference}. The endpoint difference equals $\delta Z_{T}^{\varepsilon}(Z_{T}^{X,\varepsilon,\circ}+Z_{T}^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ})$ and is $O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{2})$ by the same path bound and the stochastic boundedness of the transformed processes. Together with \eqref{xy-realized-qv-difference}, this yields
\begin{equation}\label{numerator-convergence}
    \mathfrak{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(Z^{X,\varepsilon,\circ})-\mathfrak{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(Z^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ})=O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{4})+O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{2})+O_{\mathbb{P}}\big(\varepsilon^{2}\sqrt{\varepsilon^{2}+\Delta_{n}}\big)=o_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon).
\end{equation}
Finally, Theorems~\ref{thm:auxiliary-oracle-lse} and~\ref{thm:transfer-convergence} imply $\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}=O_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$. Together with \textbf{Step~1} and \eqref{numerator-convergence}, this gives
\[
	\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{X,\circ}-\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}=\frac{\mathfrak{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(Z^{X,\varepsilon,\circ})-\mathfrak{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(Z^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ})}{\mathfrak{D}_{n}(Z^{X,\varepsilon,\circ})}-\widehat{\beta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{Y,\circ}\frac{\mathfrak{D}_{n}(Z^{X,\varepsilon,\circ})-\mathfrak{D}_{n}(Z^{Y,\varepsilon,\circ})}{\mathfrak{D}_{n}(Z^{X,\varepsilon,\circ})}=o_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon).\qedhere
\]

label: lem:CEV-holder-continuity
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Corrected local-window approximation for the target CEV process

title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{Step~1 (Uniform positive moments)}: Following the stopping argument in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:auxiliary-pseudo-cir-bounds}, define $\tau_{m}:=\inf\{t\geq0:X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\geq m\}$ for $m>x_{0}$. For $p\geq2$, H\"{o}lder's and BDG inequalities applied to the stopped SDE, together with $x^{p\vartheta_{0}}\leq1+x^{p}$, give
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq r\leq t}\big(X_{r\wedge\tau_{m}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{p}
    \Big]\leq C_{p}\Big(1+\int_{0}^{t}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq r\leq s}\big(X_{r\wedge\tau_{m}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{p}\Big]ds\Big),
\]
where $C_{p}$ is independent of $m$ and $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_{0}$. Gr\"{o}nwall's inequality, nonexplosion, and Fatou's lemma therefore yield, also using Lyapunov's inequality for $0<q<2$,
\[
    \sup_{0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_{0}}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\big(X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{q}\Big]<\infty,\qquad q>0.
\]
\textbf{Step~2 (Corrected window approximation)}: For $0\leq u\leq h_{n}$, applying the variation-of-constants formula to \eqref{small-noise-CEV-def} gives $X_{\tau_{n}+u}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}=e^{\mu u}X_{\tau_{n}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}+\mathfrak R_{n,u}^{\varepsilon}$, where
\[
    \mathfrak{R}_{n,u}^{\varepsilon}:=\varepsilon\nu\int_{\tau_{n}}^{\tau_{n}+u}e^{\mu(\tau_{n}+u-s)}\big(X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{\vartheta_{0}}dW_{s}.
\]
It\^{o}'s isometry and \textbf{Step~1} imply $\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}[|\mathfrak{R}_{n,u}^{\varepsilon}|^{2}]\leq C\varepsilon^{2}u$. Using $|x^{2\vartheta_{0}}-y^{2\vartheta_{0}}|\leq C(x^{2\vartheta_{0}-1}+y^{2\vartheta_{0}-1})|x-y|$ for $x,y\geq0$, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and \textbf{Step~1} yield
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\Big|\big(X_{\tau_{n}+u}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}-\big(e^{\mu u}X_{\tau_{n}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}\Big|\Big]\leq C\big(\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\big[|\mathfrak{R}_{n,u}^{\varepsilon}|^{2}\big]\big)^{1/2}\leq C\varepsilon\sqrt{u}.
\]
Since $\Phi_{n}(\vartheta_{0})=h_{n}^{-1}\int_{0}^{h_{n}}e^{2\mu\vartheta_{0}u}du$, integration gives
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\Big|\frac{1}{h_{n}}\int_{\tau_{n}}^{\tau_{n}'}\big(X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}ds-\big(X_{\tau_{n}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}\Phi_{n}(\vartheta_{0})\Big|\Big]\leq\frac{C\varepsilon}{h_{n}}\int_{0}^{h_{n}}\sqrt{u}du\leq C\varepsilon\sqrt{h_{n}}.
\]
Markov's inequality proves the assertion.

label: lem:local-RV-QV-approximation
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Approximation of local quadratic variation by realized variation

label: RV-QV-decomposition
title: Proof
body_md:
Set
\[
    M_{t}:=\varepsilon\nu\int_{0}^{t}\big(X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{\vartheta_{0}}dW_{s},\qquad A_{i}:=\int_{t_{i-1}}^{t_{i}}X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}ds.
\]
Throughout, sums run over $i=j_{n}+1,\ldots,j_{n}+m_{n}$, and $C$ is independent of $\varepsilon$ and $n$. We use the uniform positive-moment bounds established in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:CEV-holder-continuity}. Since $\Delta_{i}X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}=\mu A_{i}+\Delta_{i}M$ and $[X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}]=\langle M\rangle$, expanding the square gives
\begin{equation}\label{RV-QV-decomposition}
    \widehat{\mathcal{V}}_{\varepsilon,n}-\big\{[X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}]_{\tau_{n}'}-[X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}]_{\tau_{n}}\big\}=\mu^{2}\sum_{i}A_{i}^{2}+2\mu\sum_{i}A_{i}\Delta_{i}M+\sum_{i}\big[(\Delta_{i}M)^{2}-\Delta_{i}\langle M\rangle\big].
\end{equation}
\textbf{Step~1 (Drift-square term)}: By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and the moment bounds,
\begin{equation}\label{RV-QV-drift-square-rate}
    \mu^{2}\sum_{i}A_{i}^{2}\leq\mu^{2}\Delta_{n}\int_{\tau_{n}}^{\tau_{n}'}\big(X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2}ds=O_{\mathbb{P}}(h_{n}\Delta_{n}).
\end{equation}
\textbf{Step~2 (Cross term)}: Write $A_{i}=X_{t_{i-1}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\Delta_{n}+r_{i}$, where $r_{i}:=\int_{t_{i-1}}^{t_{i}}(X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}-X_{t_{i-1}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}})ds$. It\^{o}'s isometry and the moment bounds give
\begin{equation}\label{cross-leading-rate}
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\Big|\Delta_{n}\sum_{i}X_{t_{i-1}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\Delta_{i}M\Big|^{2}\Big]=\varepsilon^{2}\nu^{2}\Delta_{n}^{2}\sum_{i}\int_{t_{i-1}}^{t_{i}}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\big(X_{t_{i-1}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2}\big(X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}\Big]ds\leq C\varepsilon^{2}h_{n}\Delta_{n}^{2}.
\end{equation}
For the remainder, the SDE, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, and It\^{o}'s isometry imply
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\big|X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}-X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big|^{2}\Big]\leq C\big((t-s)^{2}+\varepsilon^{2}(t-s)\big).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
    &\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sum_{i}r_{i}^{2}\Big]\leq\Delta_{n}\sum_{i}\int_{t_{i-1}}^{t_{i}}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\big|X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}-X_{t_{i-1}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big|^{2}ds\leq C\big(h_{n}\Delta_{n}^{3}+\varepsilon^{2}h_{n}\Delta_{n}^{2}\big),\\
   & \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sum_{i}(\Delta_{i}M)^{2}\Big]=\varepsilon^{2}\nu^{2}\int_{\tau_{n}}^{\tau_{n}'}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\big(X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}\Big]ds\leq C\varepsilon^{2}h_{n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality therefore yields
\[
    \sum_{i}r_{i}\Delta_{i}M=O_{\mathbb{P}}\big(\varepsilon h_{n}\Delta_{n}^{3/2}+\varepsilon^{2}h_{n}\Delta_{n}\big)=o_{\mathbb{P}}\big(\varepsilon\Delta_{n}\sqrt{h_{n}}\big).
\]
Together with \eqref{cross-leading-rate}, this gives
\begin{equation}\label{RV-QV-cross-rate}
    \sum_{i}A_{i}\Delta_{i}M=O_{\mathbb{P}}\big(\varepsilon\Delta_{n}\sqrt{h_{n}}\big).
\end{equation}
\textbf{Step~3 (Martingale-square term)}: It\^{o}'s formula gives
\[
    (\Delta_{i}M)^{2}-\Delta_{i}\langle M\rangle=2\int_{t_{i-1}}^{t_{i}}(M_{s}-M_{t_{i-1}})dM_{s}.
\]
For $t_{i-1}\leq s\leq t_{i}$, the BDG inequality and the moment bounds yield $\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}[|M_{s}-M_{t_{i-1}}|^{4}]\leq C\varepsilon^{4}(s-t_{i-1})^{2}$. Hence, It\^{o}'s isometry and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\Big|\sum_{i}\big[(\Delta_{i}M)^{2}-\Delta_{i}\langle M\rangle\big]\Big|^{2}]&=4\varepsilon^{2}\nu^{2}\sum_{i}\int_{t_{i-1}}^{t_{i}}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[(M_{s}-M_{t_{i-1}})^{2}\big(X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}\Big]ds\\
    &\leq C\varepsilon^{4}\sum_{i}\int_{t_{i-1}}^{t_{i}}(s-t_{i-1})ds\leq C\varepsilon^{4}h_{n}\Delta_{n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus,
\begin{equation}\label{RV-QV-martingale-square-rate}
    \sum_{i}\big[(\Delta_{i}M)^{2}-\Delta_{i}\langle M\rangle\big]=O_{\mathbb{P}}\big(\varepsilon^{2}\sqrt{h_{n}\Delta_{n}}\big).
\end{equation}
Substituting \eqref{RV-QV-drift-square-rate}, \eqref{RV-QV-cross-rate}, and \eqref{RV-QV-martingale-square-rate} into \eqref{RV-QV-decomposition} and dividing by $\varepsilon^{2}\nu^{2}h_{n}$ proves \eqref{local-RV-QV-full-rate}.

label: normalized-rv-preliminary-expansion
title: Proof
body_md:
The normalized realized-variation error admits the decomposition
\[
    \frac{\widehat{\mathcal{V}}_{\varepsilon,n}}{\varepsilon^{2}\nu^{2}h_{n}}-\big(X_{\tau_{n}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}\Phi_{n}(\vartheta_{0})=\frac{\widehat{\mathcal{V}}_{\varepsilon,n}-\big\{[X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}]_{\tau'_{n}}-[X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}]_{\tau_{n}}\big\}}{\varepsilon^{2}\nu^{2}h_{n}
    }+\Big\{\frac{1}{h_{n}}\int_{\tau_{n}}^{\tau'_{n}}\big(X_{s}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}ds-\big(X_{\tau_{n}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}\Phi_{n}(\vartheta_{0})\Big\}.
\]
Set $U_{\varepsilon,n}:=\widehat{\mathcal V}_{\varepsilon,n}/(\varepsilon^{2}\nu^{2}h_{n})$, $r_{\varepsilon,n}:=\varepsilon\sqrt{h_{n}}+\sqrt{\Delta_{n}/h_{n}}+\Delta_{n}/(\varepsilon\sqrt{h_{n}})+\Delta_{n}/\varepsilon^{2}$. Combining Lemmas~\ref{lem:CEV-holder-continuity},~\ref{lem:local-RV-QV-approximation} gives
\begin{equation}\label{normalized-rv-preliminary-expansion}
    U_{\varepsilon,n}-\big(X_{\tau_{n}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}\Phi_{n}(\vartheta_{0})=O_{\mathbb{P}}(r_{\varepsilon,n}).
\end{equation}
Assumption~\ref{ass:A4} controls approximation and local identification: $h_{n}\to0$ controls the stochastic within-window error, while $m_{n}\to\infty$ ensures increasingly many increments within the shrinking window. The condition $|\log\mathcal{X}_{\tau}|\geq c_{0}$ ensures nondegenerate local identification, since the limiting derivative of the corrected identification map is $2\log\mathcal{X}_{\tau}$, which vanishes if $\mathcal{X}_{\tau}=1$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-deterministic-limit} and $\Phi_{n}(\vartheta_{0})\to1$, $\big(X_{\tau_{n}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\big)^{2\vartheta_{0}}\Phi_{n}(\vartheta_{0})$ converges in probability to $\mathcal{X}_{\tau}^{2\vartheta_{0}}>0$. Since $r_{\varepsilon,n}\to0$ under Assumptions~\ref{ass:A4} and~\ref{ass:A5}, $U_{\varepsilon,n}$ has the same limit. Together with $|\log\mathcal{X}_{\tau}|\geq c_{0}$, this implies $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_{\varepsilon,n})\to1$.

On $\mathcal{E}_{\varepsilon,n}$, define the logarithmic residual
\[
    g_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta):=\log U_{\varepsilon,n}-2\vartheta\log X_{\tau_{n}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}-\log\Phi_{n}(\vartheta),
\]
and extend it by $0$ outside this event. The two quantities compared in \eqref{normalized-rv-preliminary-expansion} are bounded away from $0$ with probability tending to $1$. The mean value theorem for the logarithm therefore gives
\begin{equation}\label{corrected-log-preliminary-expansion}
    g_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta_{0})=O_{\mathbb{P}}(r_{\varepsilon,n}).
\end{equation}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-deterministic-limit} and $|\log\mathcal{X}_{\tau}|\geq c_{0}$, $|\log X_{\tau_{n}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}|\geq c_{0}/2$ with probability tending to $1$. Since $\sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta}|\partial_{\vartheta}\log\Phi_{n}(\vartheta)|=O(h_{n})$, for all sufficiently large $n$, on $\mathcal{E}_{\varepsilon,n}$,
\[
    \inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta}|\partial_{\vartheta}g_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)|=\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\big|2\log X_{\tau_n}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}+\partial_\vartheta\log\Phi_n(\vartheta)\big|\geq c_{0}/2.
\]
Moreover, $\vartheta_{0}\in\Theta$ and the minimizing property of $\widetilde{\vartheta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{*}$ imply $|g_{\varepsilon,n}(\widetilde{\vartheta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{*})| \leq|g_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta_{0})|$.
Hence, on $\mathcal{E}_{\varepsilon,n}$, the mean value theorem and the triangle inequality yield
\[
    |\widetilde{\vartheta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{*}-\vartheta_{0}|\leq\frac{2}{c_{0}}\big|g_{\varepsilon,n}(\widetilde{\vartheta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{*})-g_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta_{0})\big|\leq\frac{4}{c_{0}}|g_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta_{0})|.
\]
Since $\widetilde{\vartheta}_{\varepsilon,n}=\widetilde{\vartheta}_{\varepsilon,n}^{*}$
on $\mathcal{E}_{\varepsilon,n}$ and $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_{\varepsilon,n})\to1$,
\eqref{corrected-log-preliminary-expansion} gives $\widetilde{\vartheta}_{\varepsilon,n}-\vartheta_{0}=O_{\mathbb{P}}(r_{\varepsilon,n})$.

Assumption~\ref{ass:A5} strengthens the basic joint small-noise and high-frequency regime. Together with $h_{n}\to0$ from Assumption~\ref{ass:A4}, it gives
\[
    \varepsilon\sqrt{h_{n}}=o(\varepsilon),\qquad\sqrt{\frac{\Delta_{n}}{h_{n}}}=o(\varepsilon),\qquad\frac{\Delta_{n}}{\varepsilon^2}=o(\varepsilon).
\]
The mixed term also satisfies
\[
    \frac{\Delta_{n}}{\varepsilon\sqrt{h_{n}}}=\sqrt{\frac{\Delta_{n}}{h_{n}}}\frac{\sqrt{\Delta_{n}}}{\varepsilon}=o(\varepsilon)o(1)=o(\varepsilon).
\]
Thus, $r_{\varepsilon,n}=o(\varepsilon)$, and the preceding rate bound yields
$\widetilde{\vartheta}_{\varepsilon,n}-\vartheta_{0}=o_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon)$.

name: Parameter sensitivity and plug-in equivalence

label: transform-uniform-derivative-bound
title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{Step~1 (Localization and uniform bounds)}: By Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-deterministic-limit}, there exists a compact interval $K\Subset(0,\infty)$ such that $X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}$ remains in $K$ on $[0,T]$ with probability tending to $1$. Denote this localization event by $\Omega_{K}^{\varepsilon}:=\{X_t^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_0}\in K \text{ for all }t\in[0,T]\}$, so that $\mathbb{P}(\Omega_{K}^{\varepsilon})\to1$. On $K\times\Theta$, the state mapping and its required derivatives are continuous, so
\begin{equation}\label{transform-uniform-derivative-bound}
    \sup_{(x,\vartheta)\in K\times\Theta}\big[|\mathcal{T}(x;\vartheta)|+|\partial_x\mathcal{T}(x;\vartheta)|+|\partial_{\vartheta}\mathcal{T}(x;\vartheta)|+|\partial_{x\vartheta}\mathcal{T}(x;\vartheta)|\big]<\infty.
\end{equation}
For $Z_{t_{i}}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)=\mathcal{T}(X_{t_{i}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}};\vartheta)$, write $\dot{Z}_{t_{i}}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta):=\partial_{\vartheta}\mathcal{T}(X_{t_{i}}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}};\vartheta)$. The preceding bound gives
\begin{equation}\label{uniform-Z-Zdot-bound}
    \sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\max_{0\leq i\leq n}\big(|Z_{t_{i}}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)|+|\dot{Z}_{t_{i}}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)|\big)=O_{\mathbb{P}}(1).
\end{equation}
Moreover, the SDE, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, It\^{o}'s isometry, and
\eqref{X-Y-uniform-second-moment} yield
\[
    \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{P}}\Big[\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\Delta_{i}X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}|^{2}\Big]\leq C(\varepsilon^{2}+\Delta_{n}).
\]
On $\Omega_{K}^{\varepsilon}$, the mean value theorem and \eqref{transform-uniform-derivative-bound} give
\[
    |\Delta_{i}Z^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)|+|\Delta_{i}\dot{Z}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)|\leq C|\Delta_{i}X^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_0}|,\qquad\vartheta\in\Theta,
\]
with $C$ independent of $\vartheta$, $\varepsilon$, and $n$. Squaring and summing, the preceding moment estimate, Markov's inequality, and $\mathbb{P}(\Omega_{K}^{\varepsilon})\to1$ imply
\begin{equation}\label{uniform-Z-increment-bound}
    \sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(|\Delta_{i}Z^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)|^{2}+|\Delta_{i}\dot{Z}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)|^{2}\big)=O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{2}+\Delta_{n}).
\end{equation}
\textbf{Step~2 (Denominator and numerator)}: Define
\[
    \mathscr{D}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta):=\Delta_{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(Z_{t_{i-1}}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)\big)^{2},\qquad\partial_{\vartheta}\mathscr{D}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)=2\Delta_{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}Z_{t_{i-1}}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)\dot{Z}_{t_{i-1}}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta).
\]
Since $n\Delta_{n}=T$, \eqref{uniform-Z-Zdot-bound} implies $\sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta}|\partial_{\vartheta}\mathscr{D}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)|=O_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$. By continuity and strict positivity on $K\times\Theta$, $c_{d}:=T\min_{(x,\vartheta)\in K\times\Theta}\mathcal{T}(x;\vartheta)^{2}>0$. On $\Omega_{K}^{\varepsilon}$, $(Z_{t_{i-1}}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta))^{2}\geq c_{d}/T$ for every $i$ and $\vartheta\in\Theta$. Since $n\Delta_{n}=T$,
\[
    \inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\mathscr{D}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)\geq\Delta_{n}n\cdot c_{d}/T=c_{d}.
\]
Consequently, $\mathbb{P}(\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\mathscr{D}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)\geq c_{d})\to1$. By \eqref{discrete-integration-by-parts-square}, the numerator of $\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,n}$ and its derivative can be written as 
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \mathscr{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)&=\alpha_{\varepsilon}\Delta_{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}Z_{t_{i-1}}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)-\frac{1}{2}\Big[\big(Z_{T}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)\big)^{2}-\big(Z_{0}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)\big)^{2}-\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(\Delta_{i}Z^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)\big)^{2}\Big],\\
    \partial_{\vartheta}\mathscr{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)&=\alpha_{\varepsilon}\Delta_{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\dot{Z}_{t_{i-1}}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)-Z_{T}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)\dot{Z}_{T}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)+Z_{0}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)\dot{Z}_{0}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Delta_{i}Z^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)\Delta_{i}\dot{Z}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta).
\end{aligned}
\]
Using $2|xy|\leq x^{2}+y^{2}$ and \eqref{uniform-Z-increment-bound}, we obtain
\[
    \sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\Big|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Delta_{i}Z^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)\Delta_{i}\dot{Z}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)\Big|\leq\frac{1}{2}\sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(|\Delta_{i}Z^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)|^{2}+|\Delta_{i}\dot{Z}^{X,\varepsilon}(\vartheta)|^{2}\big)=O_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon^{2}+\Delta_{n}).
\]
By \eqref{uniform-Z-Zdot-bound}, $n\Delta_{n}=T$, and $\alpha_{\varepsilon}=O(\varepsilon^{2})$, the first terms in $\mathscr{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)$ and $\partial_{\vartheta}\mathscr{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)$ are uniformly $O_{\mathbb P}(\varepsilon^2)$, while the endpoint terms are uniformly $O_{\mathbb P}(1)$. The squared-increment sum is controlled by \eqref{uniform-Z-increment-bound}. Thus,
\[
    \sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta}|\partial_\vartheta\mathscr{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)|=O_{\mathbb{P}}(1),\qquad\sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta}|\mathscr{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)|=O_{\mathbb{P}}(1).
\]
\textbf{Step~3 (Parameter sensitivity and plug-in equivalence)}: Since $\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,n}=\mathscr{N}_{\varepsilon,n}/\mathscr{D}_{\varepsilon,n}$, the quotient rule gives
\[
    \partial_{\vartheta}\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)=\frac{\partial_{\vartheta}\mathscr{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)}{\mathscr{D}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)}-\frac{\mathscr{N}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)\partial_{\vartheta}\mathscr{D}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)}{\mathscr{D}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)^{2}}.
\]
The bounds in \textbf{Step~2} imply $\sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta}|\partial_{\vartheta}\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)|=O_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$.

Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:A4} and~\ref{ass:A5}, Theorem~\ref{thm:preliminary-estimator-rate} gives $\widetilde\vartheta_{\varepsilon,n}-\vartheta_{0}=o_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon)$. Since $\Theta$ is an interval containing both $\widetilde\vartheta_{\varepsilon,n}$ and $\vartheta_{0}$, the mean value theorem yields
\[
    \big|\widehat\beta_{\varepsilon,n}-\widehat\beta_{\varepsilon,n}^{X,\circ}\big|\leq\sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta}|\partial_{\vartheta}\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)||\widetilde\vartheta_{\varepsilon,n}-\vartheta_{0}|=o_{\mathbb{P}}(\varepsilon).\qedhere
\]

title: Remark
body_md:
The parameter-sensitivity analysis is local in the state variable. Although $\mathcal{T}(x;\vartheta)$ is smooth in $\vartheta$ for $x>0$, the increment bounds established above require the mixed derivative $\partial_{x\vartheta}\mathcal{T}(x;\vartheta)$, which is singular as $x\downarrow0$. We therefore work on localization sets bounded away from $0$. On the other hand, the deterministic limit
$\mathcal{X}_{t}=x_{0}e^{\mu t}$ satisfies
$\inf_{0\leq t\leq T}\mathcal{X}_{t}>0$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-deterministic-limit}, there exists a compact
interval $K\Subset(0,\infty)$ such that $\mathbb{P}\big(X_{t}^{\varepsilon,\vartheta_{0}}\in K \text{ for all }t\in[0,T]\big)\to1$. Since $\Theta\Subset(1/2,1)$, all derivatives of $\mathcal{T}$ required in the sensitivity analysis are uniformly bounded on $K\times\Theta$. Hence, on these high-probability localization sets, $\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta)$ is differentiable in $\vartheta$, and the mean-value argument comparing $\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,n}(\widetilde{\vartheta}_{\varepsilon,n})$ and $\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon,n}(\vartheta_{0})$ is justified.
